ticket.title: storypole migrate never says it changes the store layout, so a single-repo project reads the dry run as a no-op
ticket.description:
MEASURED 2026-11-12 in aerofoil, a 99-ticket store still on the pre-ADR-0010 layout, and by reading the suite at 6623ebf.

The verb that performs the layout migration does not say that it does. migrate is the command that converts ledger.jsonl into tickets/<KEY>.json plus ledger-archive/ledger-migrated.jsonl (migrate/apply.rs: write every record, replay-verify each destination, archive the ledger last), which ADR 0010 makes the storage contract. Its only user-visible description, crates/storypole-cli/src/args.rs:134, is a sentence about distributing to repositories:

  Split one store's tickets into the repositories that own them

Nothing there says the storage format changes, and nothing in the run says it either.

The dry run reports the layout it is IN, never the one it will leave. migrate_cmds.rs:44 emits layout Ledger, staying 99, moving 0, adopted 0, and the human table prints only KEY / DESTINATION / EVIDENCE. With zero moves the closing line is "dry run: nothing was written and the ledger is untouched", which reads as nothing to do - for exactly the repository that most needs the change. Applying it wrote 99 records and archived a 540-event ledger.

The blindness is symmetric. A multi-repo store saw 191 moves (ADR 0010 records 191 of 350) and was still never told the format changed underneath; a single-repo store sees 0 moves and is told nothing happened at all. In both cases the only way to learn what the verb does is to read migrate/apply.rs, or to compare a migrated sibling repository afterwards.

Related drift, same reading: workspace_args.rs:19 describes `workspace distribute` as "Distribute scoped tasks from root ledger into their respective repository ledgers". The root-ledger wording predates ADR 0010 and makes a second verb read as though it performs migrate's stated purpose.

Cost, named honestly: a reader who trusts --help concludes migrate does not apply to a single-repository project. aerofoil's own migration ticket recorded its plan as 0 moving and had to reconstruct the mechanism from the source and from colinwolff.dev's post-migration store; the ticket text hedged about which effects the command had, because the help text could not answer.

Not in scope: changing what migrate does. The engine's three phases and the archive-last ordering are right; this is about the command telling the truth about itself.
acceptance_criteria: migrate --dry-run names the transition (Ledger -> Records) and the number of records it will write, in both the table and --json
migrate --help documents both effects: the layout change and the repository split
a store where every ticket stays at the root no longer closes with output that reads as nothing to do
workspace distribute --help drops the root-ledger wording that predates ADR 0010

--- a/CHANGELOG.md

@@ -9,6 +9,9 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 ## [Unreleased]
 
 ### Fixed
+- `storypole-cli`: `migrate` now reports both of its effects. The dry run names the layout transition (`Ledger -> Records`), the number of records applying would write, and where the ledger will be archived, in the table and in `--json` (`layout`, `target`, `records`); `--help` describes the layout change as well as the repository split; and a store where every ticket stays at the root no longer closes with "nothing was written and the ledger is untouched", which read as nothing to do for exactly the repository that most needed converting. A single-repository store previously saw `moving 0` while applying wrote every record and archived its ledger. `--dry-run` remains read-only. [GB-357]
+- `storypole-cli`: `workspace distribute --help` no longer describes itself as moving tasks "from root ledger into their respective repository ledgers", wording that predates the Records layout and made a second verb read like `migrate`. [GB-357]
+- `storypole-cli`: `add` now splits `--files`, `--symbols` and `--labels` on commas exactly as `update` does, and both verbs accept both spellings (`--files`/`--file`, `--symbols`/`--symbol`, `--labels`/`--label`). A comma-joined value used to be stored as one scope entry, so `--files a.rs,b.rs` produced a single path that exists nowhere while `update` produced two - the damage landed in the record and survived until somebody read it, which is how a sibling project filed a ticket naming two files as `["AGENTS.md,.gaugeblock/config.toml"]`. Criteria stay repeatable-only and are not comma-split: one criterion containing a comma is one criterion. [GB-359]
 - `storypole-core`: `event_timestamp` now reads `HandoffRecorded` from the packet's own `timestamp_ms` instead of letting it fall through to the zero arm of the timestamp table, so a handoff no longer sorts ahead of every real event. Replay by `(timestamp, id)` and replay from a legacy ledger's file order now agree, which is what `migrate` checks before it archives a ledger. Before this, any store holding a handed-off ticket that was never subsequently verified could not be migrated: `migrate` aborted with a divergence error and the written record reported the stale status (SP-54).
 - `storypole-core`: `claim` now creates and checks out the lease branch in the repository that owns the task (`scope.repo`) instead of the store root, so claiming a member task can no longer switch a harness checkout onto a feature branch; harness-level tasks record the branch without touching any checkout, and verification receipts read branch/SHA from the task's own repository (GB-137).

diff --git a/crates/storypole-cli/tests/add_update_scope_parity.rs b/crates/storypole-cli/tests/add_update_scope_parity.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..6efb5e7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/crates/storypole-cli/tests/add_update_scope_parity.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,180 @@
+//! `add` and `update` must read identical arguments identically (`GB-359`).
+//!
+//! The original defect was not a missing split but a disagreement: `update` split `--file a,b` on commas and
+//! `add` stored it as one path, so a record created the way people create records carried a scope entry that
+//! exists nowhere - `["AGENTS.md,.gaugeblock/config.toml"]` for a ticket naming two files. It survived until
+//! somebody read the file, because a populated-looking scope is not obviously wrong.
+//!
+//! These tests run the built binary twice with the same arguments and compare what was stored, which is the
+//! only comparison that would have caught it: unit-testing each verb's parser separately passes while the two
+//! parsers disagree.
+
+#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]
+
+use std::path::Path;
+use std::process::Command;
+
+const BIN: &str = env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_storypole");
+
+/// A store initialised in a temp directory.
+fn store() -> tempfile::TempDir {
+    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
+    let output = Command::new(BIN)
+        .arg("init")
+        .current_dir(dir.path())
+        .output()
+        .expect("storypole spawns");
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "init failed: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+    dir
+}
+
+/// Runs the binary and returns stdout, asserting success.
+fn run(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> String {
+    let output = Command::new(BIN)
+        .args(args)
+        .current_dir(dir)
+        .output()
+        .expect("storypole spawns");
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "storypole {args:?} failed: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string()
+}
+
+/// A ticket as the CLI reads it back.
+///
+/// Read through `show` rather than from `tickets/<KEY>.json`: a fresh store may be in Index storage and write no
+/// records at all, and the assertion is about what the verbs stored, not about which layout stored it.
+fn task_of(root: &Path, key: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
+    let out = run(root, &["show", key, "--json"]);
+    let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&out).expect("show --json is JSON");
+    value["briefing"]["task"].clone()
+}
+
+/// The `scope` object of a ticket.
+fn scope_of(root: &Path, key: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
+    task_of(root, key)["scope"].clone()
+}
+
+/// The key out of `Created task SP-1 [Bug] P3: ...`.
+fn key_from_add(stdout: &str) -> String {
+    stdout
+        .split_whitespace()
+        .nth(2)
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no key in {stdout}"))
+        .to_string()
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn identical_arguments_produce_identical_scope() {
+    let dir = store();
+
+    // Created with the comma form, which is what a person types.
+    let added = run(
+        dir.path(),
+        &[
+            "add",
+            "one",
+            "--files",
+            "a.rs,b.rs",
+            "--symbols",
+            "alpha,beta",
+            "--labels",
+            "storypole,cli",
+        ],
+    );
+    let created = key_from_add(&added);
+
+    // Created bare, then updated with the same arguments.
+    let plain = run(dir.path(), &["add", "two"]);
+    let updated = key_from_add(&plain);
+    run(
+        dir.path(),
+        &[
+            "update",
+            &updated,
+            "--files",
+            "a.rs,b.rs",
+            "--symbols",
+            "alpha,beta",
+            "--labels",
+            "storypole,cli",
+        ],
+    );
+
+    let from_add = scope_of(dir.path(), &created);
+    let from_update = scope_of(dir.path(), &updated);
+    assert_eq!(
+        from_add["target_files"], from_update["target_files"],
+        "add and update must split --files the same way"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        from_add["target_symbols"], from_update["target_symbols"],
+        "and --symbols"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(from_add["labels"], from_update["labels"], "and --labels");
+    // The specific damage: one concatenated entry instead of two usable ones.
+    assert_eq!(
+        from_add["target_files"],
+        serde_json::json!(["a.rs", "b.rs"])
+    );
+    assert_eq!(from_add["labels"], serde_json::json!(["storypole", "cli"]));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn the_singular_spelling_is_accepted_by_both_verbs() {
+    // `update` documented `--file` and `add` rejected it, so a person switching verbs hit a parse error for an
+    // argument they had just used successfully. Both spellings now reach the same field.
+    let dir = store();
+    let added = run(
+        dir.path(),
+        &["add", "one", "--file", "a.rs", "--file", "b.rs"],
+    );
+    let created = key_from_add(&added);
+    assert_eq!(
+        scope_of(dir.path(), &created)["target_files"],
+        serde_json::json!(["a.rs", "b.rs"]),
+        "repetition still works, and it is the same field as the plural"
+    );
+
+    let plain = run(dir.path(), &["add", "two"]);
+    let updated = key_from_add(&plain);
+    run(dir.path(), &["update", &updated, "--files", "a.rs,b.rs"]);
+    assert_eq!(
+        scope_of(dir.path(), &created)["target_files"],
+        scope_of(dir.path(), &updated)["target_files"],
+        "a repeated singular and a comma-separated plural agree"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn criteria_stay_repeatable_only_because_they_are_prose() {
+    // Deliberately NOT comma-split (`GB-250`): one criterion containing a comma is one criterion. This asserts
+    // the asymmetry is a decision rather than an oversight left behind by the fix above.
+    let dir = store();
+    let added = run(
+        dir.path(),
+        &[
+            "add",
+            "one",
+            "--criterion",
+            "it works, and it says so",
+            "--criterion",
+            "second",
+        ],
+    );
+    let created = key_from_add(&added);
+    let task = task_of(dir.path(), &created);
+    assert_eq!(task["scope"]["target_files"], serde_json::json!([]));
+    assert_eq!(
+        task["acceptance_criteria"],
+        serde_json::json!(["it works, and it says so", "second"]),
+        "the comma stayed inside the criterion"
+    );
+}

index 0000000..00656a7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/crates/storypole-cli/tests/migrate_reports_layout.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,163 @@
+//! `migrate` must describe both of its effects (`GB-357`).
+//!
+//! The command converts a store from one `ledger.jsonl` to a file per ticket, and also splits tickets across
+//! repositories. Only the second was ever visible: a single-repository store saw `moving 0` and a closing line
+//! about nothing being written, while applying it wrote every record and archived the ledger. The repository
+//! that most needed the change was the one told there was nothing to do.
+//!
+//! The assertion that matters is not the wording but the arithmetic: the number the dry run promises must be the
+//! number applying writes.
+
+#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]
+
+use std::fs;
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+use std::process::Command;
+
+const BIN: &str = env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_storypole");
+
+/// Runs the binary, asserting success, and returns stdout.
+fn run(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> String {
+    let output = Command::new(BIN)
+        .args(args)
+        .current_dir(dir)
+        .output()
+        .expect("storypole spawns");
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "storypole {args:?} failed: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string()
+}
+
+/// A store on the Ledger layout holding `tickets` tickets, none of which names a repository.
+fn ledger_store(tickets: usize) -> tempfile::TempDir {
+    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
+    run(dir.path(), &["init"]);
+    for index in 0..tickets {
+        run(dir.path(), &["add", &format!("ticket {index}")]);
+    }
+    dir
+}
+
+/// The store directory, whichever layout name `init` chose.
+fn dot_dir(root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
+    for candidate in [".gaugeblock/storypole", ".storypole"] {
+        let dir = root.join(candidate);
+        if dir.is_dir() {
+            return dir;
+        }
+    }
+    panic!("no store under {}", root.display());
+}
+
+/// The `key: value` numbers out of the dry run's JSON.
+fn json_field(json: &str, field: &str) -> String {
+    let needle = format!("\"{field}\":");
+    let start = json
+        .find(&needle)
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no {field} in {json}"))
+        + needle.len();
+    json[start..]
+        .trim_start_matches('"')
+        .chars()
+        .take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
+        .collect()
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn the_dry_run_names_the_transition_and_the_record_count() {
+    let dir = ledger_store(3);
+
+    let json = run(dir.path(), &["migrate", "--dry-run", "--json"]);
+    assert_eq!(json_field(&json, "layout"), "Ledger");
+    assert_eq!(
+        json_field(&json, "target"),
+        "Records",
+        "the dry run must name the layout it will leave, not only the one it is in: {json}"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(json_field(&json, "records"), "3");
+    assert_eq!(
+        json_field(&json, "moving"),
+        "0",
+        "this store has one repository, so nothing moves - which is the case that read as a no-op"
+    );
+
+    let table = run(dir.path(), &["migrate", "--dry-run"]);
+    assert!(
+        table.contains("Ledger -> Records"),
+        "the table must show the transition: {table}"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        table.contains("3 record(s)"),
+        "and the number of records: {table}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_store_with_no_moves_still_says_what_applying_would_do() {
+    let dir = ledger_store(2);
+    let table = run(dir.path(), &["migrate", "--dry-run"]);
+    assert!(
+        !table.contains("nothing was written and the ledger is untouched"),
+        "the old closing line read as a no-op for exactly the store that needed the migration: {table}"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        table.contains("change the layout"),
+        "a zero-move store must be told the format changes: {table}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn the_promised_record_count_is_what_applying_writes() {
+    // The wording is the symptom; this is the defect. If the preview and the write disagree, a reader who trusts
+    // the dry run is misinformed no matter how clearly it is phrased.
+    let dir = ledger_store(3);
+    let promised: usize = json_field(
+        &run(dir.path(), &["migrate", "--dry-run", "--json"]),
+        "records",
+    )
+    .parse()
+    .expect("records is a number");
+
+    run(dir.path(), &["migrate"]);
+    let tickets = dot_dir(dir.path()).join("tickets");
+    let written = fs::read_dir(&tickets)
+        .expect("a tickets directory after migrating")
+        .flatten()
+        .filter(|entry| entry.path().extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "json"))
+        .count();
+
+    assert_eq!(promised, written, "the dry run promised {promised}");
+    assert!(
+        dot_dir(dir.path())
+            .join("ledger-archive/ledger-migrated.jsonl")
+            .is_file(),
+        "and the ledger is archived, which is the other half the dry run now names"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn help_documents_both_effects() {
+    let dir = ledger_store(0);
+    let help = run(dir.path(), &["migrate", "--help"]);
+    assert!(
+        help.contains("Records layout"),
+        "the verb that performs the layout migration must say so: {help}"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        help.contains("repositories that own them"),
+        "and must keep saying it splits the tickets: {help}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn workspace_distribute_no_longer_reads_as_the_layout_migration() {
+    let dir = ledger_store(0);
+    let help = run(dir.path(), &["workspace", "--help"]);
+    assert!(
+        !help.contains("root ledger"),
+        "the root-ledger wording predates the Records layout and makes distribute read like migrate: {help}"
+    );
+}

task.title: storypole migrate never says it changes the store layout, so a single-repo project reads the dry run as a no-op
task.description:
MEASURED 2026-11-12 in aerofoil, a 99-ticket store still on the pre-ADR-0010 layout, and by reading the suite at 6623ebf.

The verb that performs the layout migration does not say that it does. migrate is the command that converts ledger.jsonl into tickets/<KEY>.json plus ledger-archive/ledger-migrated.jsonl (migrate/apply.rs: write every record, replay-verify each destination, archive the ledger last), which ADR 0010 makes the storage contract. Its only user-visible description, crates/storypole-cli/src/args.rs:134, is a sentence about distributing to repositories:

  Split one store's tickets into the repositories that own them

Nothing there says the storage format changes, and nothing in the run says it either.

The dry run reports the layout it is IN, never the one it will leave. migrate_cmds.rs:44 emits layout Ledger, staying 99, moving 0, adopted 0, and the human table prints only KEY / DESTINATION / EVIDENCE. With zero moves the closing line is "dry run: nothing was written and the ledger is untouched", which reads as nothing to do - for exactly the repository that most needs the change. Applying it wrote 99 records and archived a 540-event ledger.

The blindness is symmetric. A multi-repo store saw 191 moves (ADR 0010 records 191 of 350) and was still never told the format changed underneath; a single-repo store sees 0 moves and is told nothing happened at all. In both cases the only way to learn what the verb does is to read migrate/apply.rs, or to compare a migrated sibling repository afterwards.

Related drift, same reading: workspace_args.rs:19 describes `workspace distribute` as "Distribute scoped tasks from root ledger into their respective repository ledgers". The root-ledger wording predates ADR 0010 and makes a second verb read as though it performs migrate's stated purpose.

Cost, named honestly: a reader who trusts --help concludes migrate does not apply to a single-repository project. aerofoil's own migration ticket recorded its plan as 0 moving and had to reconstruct the mechanism from the source and from colinwolff.dev's post-migration store; the ticket text hedged about which effects the command had, because the help text could not answer.

Not in scope: changing what migrate does. The engine's three phases and the archive-last ordering are right; this is about the command telling the truth about itself.
acceptance_criteria: migrate --dry-run names the transition (Ledger -> Records) and the number of records it will write, in both the table and --json
migrate --help documents both effects: the layout change and the repository split
a store where every ticket stays at the root no longer closes with output that reads as nothing to do
workspace distribute --help drops the root-ledger wording that predates ADR 0010

+//! `add` and `update` must read identical arguments identically (`GB-359`).
+//!
+//! The original defect was not a missing split but a disagreement: `update` split `--file a,b` on commas and
+//! `add` stored it as one path, so a record created the way people create records carried a scope entry that
+//! exists nowhere - `["AGENTS.md,.gaugeblock/config.toml"]` for a ticket naming two files. It survived until
+//! somebody read the file, because a populated-looking scope is not obviously wrong.
+//!
+//! These tests run the built binary twice with the same arguments and compare what was stored, which is the
+//! only comparison that would have caught it: unit-testing each verb's parser separately passes while the two
+//! parsers disagree.
+
+#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]
+
+use std::path::Path;
+use std::process::Command;
+
+const BIN: &str = env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_storypole");
+
+/// A store initialised in a temp directory.
+fn store() -> tempfile::TempDir {
+    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
+    let output = Command::new(BIN)
+        .arg("init")
+        .current_dir(dir.path())
+        .output()
+        .expect("storypole spawns");
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "init failed: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+    dir
+}
+
+/// Runs the binary and returns stdout, asserting success.
+fn run(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> String {
+    let output = Command::new(BIN)
+        .args(args)
+        .current_dir(dir)
+        .output()
+        .expect("storypole spawns");
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "storypole {args:?} failed: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string()
+}
+
+/// A ticket as the CLI reads it back.
+///
+/// Read through `show` rather than from `tickets/<KEY>.json`: a fresh store may be in Index storage and write no
+/// records at all, and the assertion is about what the verbs stored, not about which layout stored it.
+fn task_of(root: &Path, key: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
+    let out = run(root, &["show", key, "--json"]);
+    let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&out).expect("show --json is JSON");
+    value["briefing"]["task"].clone()
+}
+
+/// The `scope` object of a ticket.
+fn scope_of(root: &Path, key: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
+    task_of(root, key)["scope"].clone()
+}
+
+/// The key out of `Created task SP-1 [Bug] P3: ...`.
+fn key_from_add(stdout: &str) -> String {
+    stdout
+        .split_whitespace()
+        .nth(2)
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no key in {stdout}"))
+        .to_string()
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn identical_arguments_produce_identical_scope() {
+    let dir = store();
+
+    // Created with the comma form, which is what a person types.
+    let added = run(
+        dir.path(),
+        &[
+            "add",
+            "one",
+            "--files",
+            "a.rs,b.rs",
+            "--symbols",
+            "alpha,beta",
+            "--labels",
+            "storypole,cli",
+        ],
+    );
+    let created = key_from_add(&added);
+
+    // Created bare, then updated with the same arguments.
+    let plain = run(dir.path(), &["add", "two"]);
+    let updated = key_from_add(&plain);
+    run(
+        dir.path(),
+        &[
+            "update",
+            &updated,
+            "--files",
+            "a.rs,b.rs",
+            "--symbols",
+            "alpha,beta",
+            "--labels",
+            "storypole,cli",
+        ],
+    );
+
+    let from_add = scope_of(dir.path(), &created);
+    let from_update = scope_of(dir.path(), &updated);
+    assert_eq!(
+        from_add["target_files"], from_update["target_files"],
+        "add and update must split --files the same way"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        from_add["target_symbols"], from_update["target_symbols"],
+        "and --symbols"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(from_add["labels"], from_update["labels"], "and --labels");
+    // The specific damage: one concatenated entry instead of two usable ones.
+    assert_eq!(
+        from_add["target_files"],
+        serde_json::json!(["a.rs", "b.rs"])
+    );
+    assert_eq!(from_add["labels"], serde_json::json!(["storypole", "cli"]));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn the_singular_spelling_is_accepted_by_both_verbs() {
+    // `update` documented `--file` and `add` rejected it, so a person switching verbs hit a parse error for an
+    // argument they had just used successfully. Both spellings now reach the same field.
+    let dir = store();
+    let added = run(
+        dir.path(),
+        &["add", "one", "--file", "a.rs", "--file", "b.rs"],
+    );
+    let created = key_from_add(&added);
+    assert_eq!(
+        scope_of(dir.path(), &created)["target_files"],
+        serde_json::json!(["a.rs", "b.rs"]),
+        "repetition still works, and it is the same field as the plural"
+    );
+
+    let plain = run(dir.path(), &["add", "two"]);
+    let updated = key_from_add(&plain);
+    run(dir.path(), &["update", &updated, "--files", "a.rs,b.rs"]);
+    assert_eq!(
+        scope_of(dir.path(), &created)["target_files"],
+        scope_of(dir.path(), &updated)["target_files"],
+        "a repeated singular and a comma-separated plural agree"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn criteria_stay_repeatable_only_because_they_are_prose() {
+    // Deliberately NOT comma-split (`GB-250`): one criterion containing a comma is one criterion. This asserts
+    // the asymmetry is a decision rather than an oversight left behind by the fix above.
+    let dir = store();
+    let added = run(
+        dir.path(),
+        &[
+            "add",
+            "one",
+            "--criterion",
+            "it works, and it says so",
+            "--criterion",
+            "second",
+        ],
+    );
+    let created = key_from_add(&added);
+    let task = task_of(dir.path(), &created);
+    assert_eq!(task["scope"]["target_files"], serde_json::json!([]));
+    assert_eq!(
+        task["acceptance_criteria"],
+        serde_json::json!(["it works, and it says so", "second"]),
+        "the comma stayed inside the criterion"
+    );
+}
diff --git a/crates/storypole-cli/tests/migrate_reports_layout.rs b/crates/storypole-cli/tests/migrate_reports_layout.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..00656a7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/crates/storypole-cli/tests/migrate_reports_layout.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,163 @@
+//! `migrate` must describe both of its effects (`GB-357`).
+//!
+//! The command converts a store from one `ledger.jsonl` to a file per ticket, and also splits tickets across
+//! repositories. Only the second was ever visible: a single-repository store saw `moving 0` and a closing line
+//! about nothing being written, while applying it wrote every record and archived the ledger. The repository
+//! that most needed the change was the one told there was nothing to do.
+//!
+//! The assertion that matters is not the wording but the arithmetic: the number the dry run promises must be the
+//! number applying writes.
+
+#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]
+
+use std::fs;
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+use std::process::Command;
+
+const BIN: &str = env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_storypole");
+
+/// Runs the binary, asserting success, and returns stdout.
+fn run(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> String {
+    let output = Command::new(BIN)
+        .args(args)
+        .current_dir(dir)
+        .output()
+        .expect("storypole spawns");
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "storypole {args:?} failed: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string()
+}
+
+/// A store on the Ledger layout holding `tickets` tickets, none of which names a repository.
+fn ledger_store(tickets: usize) -> tempfile::TempDir {
+    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
+    run(dir.path(), &["init"]);
+    for index in 0..tickets {
+        run(dir.path(), &["add", &format!("ticket {index}")]);
+    }
+    dir
+}
+
+/// The store directory, whichever layout name `init` chose.
+fn dot_dir(root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
+    for candidate in [".gaugeblock/storypole", ".storypole"] {
+        let dir = root.join(candidate);
+        if dir.is_dir() {
+            return dir;
+        }
+    }
+    panic!("no store under {}", root.display());
+}
+
+/// The `key: value` numbers out of the dry run's JSON.
+fn json_field(json: &str, field: &str) -> String {
+    let needle = format!("\"{field}\":");
+    let start = json
+        .find(&needle)
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no {field} in {json}"))
+        + needle.len();
+    json[start..]
+        .trim_start_matches('"')
+        .chars()
+        .take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
+        .collect()
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn the_dry_run_names_the_transition_and_the_record_count() {
+    let dir = ledger_store(3);
+
+    let json = run(dir.path(), &["migrate", "--dry-run", "--json"]);
+    assert_eq!(json_field(&json, "layout"), "Ledger");
+    assert_eq!(
+        json_field(&json, "target"),
+        "Records",
+        "the dry run must name the layout it will leave, not only the one it is in: {json}"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(json_field(&json, "records"), "3");
+    assert_eq!(
+        json_field(&json, "moving"),
+        "0",
+        "this store has one repository, so nothing moves - which is the case that read as a no-op"
+    );
+
+    let table = run(dir.path(), &["migrate", "--dry-run"]);
+    assert!(
+        table.contains("Ledger -> Records"),
+        "the table must show the transition: {table}"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        table.contains("3 record(s)"),
+        "and the number of records: {table}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_store_with_no_moves_still_says_what_applying_would_do() {
+    let dir = ledger_store(2);
+    let table = run(dir.path(), &["migrate", "--dry-run"]);
+    assert!(
+        !table.contains("nothing was written and the ledger is untouched"),
+        "the old closing line read as a no-op for exactly the store that needed the migration: {table}"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        table.contains("change the layout"),
+        "a zero-move store must be told the format changes: {table}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn the_promised_record_count_is_what_applying_writes() {
+    // The wording is the symptom; this is the defect. If the preview and the write disagree, a reader who trusts
+    // the dry run is misinformed no matter how clearly it is phrased.
+    let dir = ledger_store(3);
+    let promised: usize = json_field(
+        &run(dir.path(), &["migrate", "--dry-run", "--json"]),
+        "records",
+    )
+    .parse()
+    .expect("records is a number");
+
+    run(dir.path(), &["migrate"]);
+    let tickets = dot_dir(dir.path()).join("tickets");
+    let written = fs::read_dir(&tickets)
+        .expect("a tickets directory after migrating")
+        .flatten()
+        .filter(|entry| entry.path().extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "json"))
+        .count();
+
+    assert_eq!(promised, written, "the dry run promised {promised}");
+    assert!(
+        dot_dir(dir.path())
+            .join("ledger-archive/ledger-migrated.jsonl")
+            .is_file(),
+        "and the ledger is archived, which is the other half the dry run now names"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn help_documents_both_effects() {
+    let dir = ledger_store(0);
+    let help = run(dir.path(), &["migrate", "--help"]);
+    assert!(
+        help.contains("Records layout"),
+        "the verb that performs the layout migration must say so: {help}"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        help.contains("repositories that own them"),
+        "and must keep saying it splits the tickets: {help}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn workspace_distribute_no_longer_reads_as_the_layout_migration() {
+    let dir = ledger_store(0);
+    let help = run(dir.path(), &["workspace", "--help"]);
+    assert!(
+        !help.contains("root ledger"),
+        "the root-ledger wording predates the Records layout and makes distribute read like migrate: {help}"
+    );
+}
